lines.heard: This clip tells a stranger my name, my building, and my phone number.
All fictional. But creators post clips like this every day.
A name on a parcel, a society board behind you, a number you say out loud.
Most redaction tools look for a fixed list, basis, license plates, screens, documents.
On my held out clips, that list found zero or four planted leaves.
So Veil asks a different question. What in this video could identify you?
Muse Spark looks at keyframes and proposes candidates, each with a reason. The notification shows a full name. The gold plate shows a surname and a flat number.
None of these is a face or a license plate. The model has to understand the scene.
SAM 3.1 tracks each one through every frame and the output covers exactly those regions.
With Spark in the loop, three of four planted leaks were found. The delivery box label was still missed.
Then code checks the work. Veil decodes its own output and confirms the covers are really there.
It re-reads the output with local OCR and runs a face detector on sampled frames.
And models make mistakes. Here Sam put the name mask on a block of code.
Local OCR. Re-reads. The mask found code instead of the name Spark claimed and threw it out.
Spoken Numbers 2. Muse Voice Transcribe. Here's a phone number read out in Hindi, and Veil mutes it.
Then it transcribes the output again. No digit run left.
But the transcript gets digits wrong and the mute window is still wider than my own limit.
That's the point. Veil never says a video is safe.
Every item is covered, unresolved or not checked and it tells you why.
Muse Spark. Two items are unresolved. Eight weren't checked because a model call failed or they hit my cost cap.
I held myself to that too. I wrote a test gate before running it. It failed. Every fix since is labeled post-gate and the gate still failed.
Send it on a clip, read the receipt and decide before you post.
Models Propose. And Code Decides. Veil. Built Solo with Muse Spark. SAM 3.1. And Muse Voice.
